review_kind: author-team curriculum and source-to-prose alignment audit
acceptance: not an independent acceptance or learner mastery certificate
method: Read canonical JSON lesson prose and HTML project/checkpoint guidance; checked substantive objective groups against explanations, independent practice, linked source and stage gates.

Used static checks for unique lesson IDs, prerequisite targets, embedded source files, @root targets, line-start Cargo commands, selected recurring lesson sections, all requirement-map targets and gate anchors. Structural markers and word counts do not establish instructional quality.

Deeply reviewed and executed the new core laboratories and owned early/final checkpoint reconstructions. Reviewed other authors' new bridge prose and recorded evidence scopes; did not rerun their entire systems, database, performance or browser verification.

Primary Rust Weak/TryInto documentation was read from the installed Rust 1.99.0 rustdoc tree after the web tool could not retrieve the corresponding versioned URLs. No browser access was attempted for this audit.

actual_owned_verification.core_labs: 13 unit tests and 3 doctests passed; strict Clippy, three examples, three reconstructed packages, no-overwrite rejection and two expected failing mutations passed.
actual_owned_verification.early_checkpoints: 21 distinct early unit tests across p01–p06 passed, with runnable demonstrations and strict Clippy. The resolved first p04 lint failure is retained.
actual_owned_verification.final_checkpoints: Six complete reference reconstructions passed cargo test. Twelve fresh early/final copies passed offline locked metadata with normalized per-checkpoint lockfiles.

findings.issue: Compound collections, standard conversion traits and interior mutability lacked focused beginner-to-middle instruction and runnable checkpoints.
findings.resolution: Added 01-collections, 02-conversions and 03-interior, complete examples and reconstruction helper, bounded contracts, meaningful tests, independent tasks, folded hints, engineering decisions and topic-specific investigations. Added actual TryInto usage, public-path doctests, a private-representation compile failure and Weak observer lifecycle test; explained strong ownership cycles without claiming the acyclic log already contains one.

findings.issue: Early main-project checkpoints were not uniformly complete source states that learners could reconstruct.
findings.resolution: Authored six genuinely smaller complete standalone milestones plus explicit final checkpoints, per-checkpoint contracts and engineering decisions, no-overwrite helper integration, and dedicated lockfiles. Earlier framing-only p06 has no persistence claim and explicitly does not recommend a weak checksum for the durable store. Source snapshots contain no build cache.

findings.issue: Several objective groups linked to stage gates were taught but not explicitly assessed there.
findings.resolution: Added concrete gates for workspace/Git/binary/program structure, collection contracts, conversion and public API evolution, RefCell/Weak lifecycle and fuzz-oracle revision, atomicity and retained futures, HTTP/browser security boundaries, semantic browser controls/rendering modes, advanced type/macro/FFI/no_std boundaries, and measured operations/rollback. Evidence requires a prediction, a discriminating experiment and justified limits; unavailable browser checks remain open.

findings.issue: Final performance assessment requested an impossible unmodified journal size.
findings.resolution: Uses 100, 1000 and near-cap workloads within the 10,000-record budget, fresh storage for each trial and explicit accounting for setup records and the exact boundary. Larger workloads require a specified architecture change.

findings.issue: 00-conversions and both new performance bridges revealed practice hints/solutions immediately.
findings.resolution: Independent specifications remain visible; hints and worked directions are separately revealed through details/summary. Performance bridge owner made its prose changes and added exact p12 reconstruction commands.

findings.issue: Earlier audit gaps in atomics, pinning, HTTP middleware/cookie/TLS boundaries, resource profiling and real fuzzing needed genuine instruction and executable evidence.
findings.resolution: Reviewed these authored bridges for concrete model, controlled example, failure experiment, scope and gate alignment. The pinned-future lesson distinguishes deadline semantics and retained state; the HTTP bridge separates authentication, authorization and browser policies; profiling distinguishes resource counters from CPU samples; fuzzing includes an intentionally false Unicode oracle and revised invariant. Their own verification logs remain authoritative, not this prose audit.

findings.issue: Requirement map omitted some actual foundational teaching locations and implied keyword coverage for TryInto/Weak before explicit practice existed.
findings.resolution: Parent aligned terminal/binary/closure/doc-test mappings; actual TryInto and Weak examples and investigation now substantiate those claims. All 83 mapped objective groups resolve to canonical lessons, a present gate and existing evidence files.

findings.issue: First p04 early checkpoint Clippy run rejected a manual flatten pattern.
findings.resolution: Used iter().flatten() for present-layer traversal without changing precedence semantics. The historical failing command remains in the log; subsequent p04 tests, execution and strict Clippy passed. This is a retained resolved failure, not a claim every historical command succeeded.

findings.issue: The requested Rayon comparison needed an explicit assessed scheduling decision alongside the existing serial/scoped-thread teaching.
findings.resolution: The new 04-parallel-tools lesson compares three actual implementations over the same bounded borrowed input; explains local pool installation, ordered outputs, I/O versus CPU work and the payload/thread budgets; avoids an unmeasured speed ranking. Gate 4 now requires an uneven fixture, complete output equality, omitted-chunk diagnosis, local-pool evidence and a workload-based selection with explicit budgets.

findings.issue: The fuzz lesson requested an associativity oracle, but its worked direction originally used explicit grouping that could not distinguish left from right subtraction association.
findings.resolution: The worked direction now compares unparenthesized a-b-c against (a-b)-c, with the concrete 8-3-2 counterexample. Root added the corresponding finite-domain property test. Explicit (a+b)*c is correctly labeled as grouping evidence. Nightly installation instructions now use mise install rust@nightly-2026-10-08, and the atomics lesson explicitly includes a non-atomic access in its data-race definition.

No browser interaction, visual layout, keyboard behavior or assistive-technology behavior was verified by this audit; saved browser access restrictions remain a separate root-owned verification limitation.
Static source paths and a stage-gate specification do not prove a learner can complete the exercise; the assessment requires observable independent work and explanation.

Native tests cover recorded input families and platforms, not arbitrary crash/power-loss behavior, every unsafe execution, production identity/TLS deployments, consensus, hardware firmware or sustained capacity. Relevant lessons explicitly limit those claims.

The shared lesson reconstruction callout and p16 storage-specific prose are integrated in canonical source. The parent owns final rendered-site regeneration and static/runtime verification. This audit covers canonical sources at the recorded hashes and does not independently repeat those integration checks.
interpretation: No additional unaddressed foundational topic or misleading completed-feature claim was identified within the reviewed canonical scope after the listed corrections. This conclusion is an author audit with stated limits; it is not a claim that browser QA, independent review or learner mastery is complete.
